segments.title: Reel opening at Don Albert's home, January 1974
segments.summary: Dick Allen identifies the reel, date and place of the interview at Albert's home.

segments.title: Jam sessions with George Foster and Deep Forest
segments.summary: Albert recalls a Chicago jam session where George Foster and others played Deep Forest with no horns, and how he came upon it.

segments.title: Wakes in Pensacola and the shirt-turning characters
segments.summary: Stories of the band attending a wake in Pensacola with Jimmy Johnson buying booze, and of Billy Douglas and Dink Taylor turning shirts inside out.

segments.title: Judge Sondas and playing the pier in St. Petersburg
segments.summary: Spelling of a judge's name, then a story from a Florida pier gig and a Pensacola dance hall with a glass floor; the text is garbled by ASR loops.

segments.title: Chauncey Holland and Al Travis as band bookers
segments.summary: Albert praises Chauncey Holland and Al Travis as salesmen who could book a band solidly, regretting that Travis was crooked.

segments.title: Baseball in New Orleans and the Negro league teams
segments.summary: The interviewer and Albert discuss New Orleans ballparks and the visiting Negro league teams Albert watched as a boy.

segments.title: Albert catching for semi-pro teams on tour
segments.summary: Albert describes catching for semi-pro teams in Texas and Ohio, advertised as the great Don Albert, and how it kept him fit and made friends.

segments.title: Musicians and sports: tennis, baseball teams and hobbies
segments.summary: Talk of other musicians who played baseball and tennis, and Albert's view that outside activity balances music.

segments.title: Alvin Wall, Ziggy Johnson and Alvin Wall's band
segments.summary: Albert praises saxophonist and bandleader Alvin Wall, mentions meeting Ziggy Johnson in Detroit, and describes the size of bands then; the passage ends in ASR loops.

segments.title: Lee Hilden, trumpeter who took to the bottle
segments.summary: Albert describes the gifted trumpeter Lee Hilden, whom he sent to Lucky Millinder, and his work with Troy Floyd and McNeil.

segments.title: Wingy Manone, George Foster and Eddie Heywood in San Antonio
segments.summary: Musicians who passed through San Antonio: Wingy Manone, George Foster who worked on Armstrong's arm, and the Heywoods.

segments.title: Keeping his lip up and Maury Maverick
segments.summary: Albert explains practising daily to keep his lip for concerts, and the favour for Maury Maverick's father, mayor of San Antonio.

segments.title: Water Gardens dance halls and band styles
segments.summary: Many dance halls shared the name Water Gardens; talk of Charleston bands and how bands copy each other.

segments.title: Female impersonator shows at the Riverside Gardens
segments.summary: Albert recalls a show of nine or ten female impersonators at the Riverside Gardens in San Antonio.

segments.title: The Keyhole club and visiting stars
segments.summary: Albert describes the Keyhole, trumpeter Come Co-lax, and Billy Eckstine, Sarah Vaughan, Armstrong and others sitting in.

segments.title: Anna Mae Winburn and singer Ann Welburn
segments.summary: Albert distinguishes bandleader Anna Mae Winburn from singer Ann Welburn, whom he coached on stage presence.
